conditionalReplacementHosts.speaker: tally
conditionalReplacementHosts.text: In a triple task, click tiles to fill three slots, then Test it. A yes does not prove your rule.

conditionalReplacementHosts.speaker: tally

conditionalReplacementHosts.speaker: tally
conditionalReplacementHosts.text: Test a triple you expect NOT to fit. If it fits, your guess needs changing. Then choose Name the rule.

conditionalReplacementHosts.speaker: tally

conditionalReplacementHosts.speaker: kuku
conditionalReplacementHosts.text: We need a safe route. These are the rules of this world, not promises about real people.

conditionalReplacementHosts.speaker: kuku
conditionalReplacementHosts.text: Click Truth or Lie under each guard. Your marks are a guess you can change.

conditionalReplacementHosts.speaker: kuku
conditionalReplacementHosts.text: Example: A says "B is a liar". Suppose A is honest: B must be a liar. Suppose A lies: B must be honest.

conditionalReplacementHosts.speaker: kuku
conditionalReplacementHosts.text: Now check the other statements. A possible answer must make every honest statement true and every lie false.

conditionalReplacementHosts.speaker: kuku
conditionalReplacementHosts.text: Choose a door and Open the gate when all your marks fit. How to play is free. The Hint button shows its heart cost. Think first, then check your answer.

conditionalReplacementHosts.text: We judge whether the conclusion MUST follow from these facts. Read the scrolls first.

conditionalReplacementHosts.speaker: kuku
conditionalReplacementHosts.text: Shade means no things here. Example: "All ducks are birds" shades the ducks-only region outside birds. It does not add an x.

conditionalReplacementHosts.speaker: kuku
conditionalReplacementHosts.text: Some means at least one. "Some ducks are birds" needs an x in their overlap. "No ducks are birds" shades that overlap.

conditionalReplacementHosts.speaker: kuku
conditionalReplacementHosts.text: Choose Shade and click a region, or drag an x from the tray. Put an x on a border when the facts leave its side open. Clear lets you restart.

conditionalReplacementHosts.speaker: kuku
conditionalReplacementHosts.text: Choose Valid only if every possible world that fits the facts also fits the conclusion. A true conclusion can still come from a bad argument.

conditionalReplacementHosts.text: The drawing is optional working. If asked, judge premise support using only the reference records, then Seal the verdict. Missing evidence is not false. How to play is free. The Hint button shows its heart cost.

conditionalReplacementHosts.speaker: narrator
conditionalReplacementHosts.text: The four boxes count right and wrong decisions. Example: refusing help to someone who needs it is a missed need, even if most other decisions are right.

conditionalReplacementHosts.speaker: narrator
conditionalReplacementHosts.text: Read the rule and budget. Name the flaw, then choose one of the listed fixes to meet the stated goals.

conditionalReplacementHosts.speaker: narrator
conditionalReplacementHosts.text: Check who your fix changes, its cost, and the mistakes left. If asked, choose a value and support it with a reason from the audit, then Hand in the audit. How to play is free. The Hint button shows its heart cost. Think first, then check your answer.

conditionalReplacementHosts.speaker: kuku
conditionalReplacementHosts.text: Find which villagers are imps. Every identity must fit all their words under these rules.

conditionalReplacementHosts.speaker: kuku
conditionalReplacementHosts.text: Click a villager to add an accusation token. Click again to remove it. Mark suspected imps; leave honest villagers unmarked.

conditionalReplacementHosts.speaker: kuku
conditionalReplacementHosts.text: Open the truth table. A row is one possible world; a column asks whether someone's words are true in that world.

conditionalReplacementHosts.speaker: kuku
conditionalReplacementHosts.text: Example: Baker says "Sweep is an imp". In a world where Sweep is honest, those words are false. Baker must then be an imp.

conditionalReplacementHosts.speaker: kuku
conditionalReplacementHosts.text: Check rows for clashes and cross out the ones that cannot fit. Put tokens on the imps in the surviving world and accuse when every statement fits. How to play is free. The Hint button shows its heart cost. Think first, then check your answer.

conditionalReplacementHosts.speaker: kuku
conditionalReplacementHosts.text: We put the argument on trial. Your job is to connect a weak statement to evidence.

conditionalReplacementHosts.speaker: kuku
conditionalReplacementHosts.text: Use the arrows to read the testimony. Press a statement to hear more; some evidence appears only after pressing.

conditionalReplacementHosts.speaker: kuku
conditionalReplacementHosts.text: Open the Court record. Read what each piece of evidence establishes, not just its picture.

conditionalReplacementHosts.speaker: kuku
conditionalReplacementHosts.text: Example: "The door stayed locked all day" clashes with a dated record showing it opened at noon. Present that record against that statement.

conditionalReplacementHosts.speaker: kuku
conditionalReplacementHosts.text: Use Present on the statement, choose evidence, then Take that. Name the flaw and repair the proof if asked. Finish with Close the case. How to play is free. The Hint button shows its heart cost. Think first, then check your answer.
